messages.content: I have updated some more functions you can choose from. What about now?

function.name: authenticate_twitter
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Authenticate a user with username and password. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: comment
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Comment on a tweet for the authenticated user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet to comment on.

function.name: follow_user
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Follow a user for the authenticated user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username_to_follow.description: Username of the user to follow.

follow_status.description: True if followed, False if already following.

function.name: get_tweet
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Retrieve a specific tweet. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet to retrieve.

tags.description: List of tags associated with the tweet.

mentions.description: List of users mentioned in the tweet.

function.name: get_tweet_comments
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Retrieve all comments for a specific tweet. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet to retrieve comments for.

comments.description: List of dictionaries, each containing comment information.

function.name: get_user_stats
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Get statistics for a specific user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username.description: Username of the user to get statistics for.

tweet_count.description: Number of tweets posted by the user.

following_count.description: Number of users the specified user is following.

retweet_count.description: Number of retweets made by the user.

function.name: get_user_tweets
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Retrieve all tweets from a specific user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username.description: Username of the user whose tweets to retrieve.

user_tweets.description: List of dictionaries, each containing tweet information.

tags.description: List of tags associated with the tweet.

mentions.description: List of users mentioned in the tweet.

function.name: list_all_following
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: List all users that the authenticated user is following. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

following_list.description: List of all users that the authenticated user is following.

function.name: mention
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Mention specified users in a tweet. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tweet_id.description: ID of the tweet where users are mentioned.

mentioned_usernames.description: List of usernames to be mentioned.

function.name: post_tweet
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Post a tweet for the authenticated user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

tags.description: List of tags for the tweet. Tag name should start with #. This is only relevant if the user wants to add tags to the tweet.

mentions.description: List of users mentioned in the tweet. Mention name should start with @. This is only relevant if the user wants to add mentions to the tweet.

tags.description: List of tags associated with the tweet.

mentions.description: List of users mentioned in the tweet.

function.name: posting_get_login_status
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Get the login status of the current user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

login_status.description: True if the current user is logged in, False otherwise.

function.name: retweet
function.description: This tool belongs to the TwitterAPI, which provides core functionality for posting tweets, retweeting, commenting, and following users on Twitter. Tool description: Retweet a tweet for the authenticated user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Create a new file of any extension in the current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the new file in the current directory. file_name is local to the current directory and does not allow path.

function.name: wc
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Count the number of lines, words, and characters in a file of any extension from current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: Name of the file of current directory to perform wc operation on.

mode.description: Mode of operation ('l' for lines, 'w' for words, 'c' for characters).

count.description: The count of the number of lines, words, or characters in the file.

type.description: The type of unit we are counting. [Enum]: ["lines", "words", "characters"]

function.name: echo
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Write content to a file at current directory or display it in the terminal.

content.description: The content to write or display.

file_name.description: The name of the file at current directory to write the content to. Defaults to None.

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.

It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Remove a directory at current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

dir_name.description: The name of the directory to remove. Directory must be local to the current directory.

result.description: The result of the remove operation.

function.name: sort
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Sort the contents of a file line by line. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the file appeared at current directory to sort.

sorted_content.description: The sorted content of the file.

function.name: tail
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Display the last part of a file of any extension. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the file to display. No path is allowed and you can only perform on file at local directory.

lines.description: The number of lines to display from the end of the file. Defaults to 10.

last_lines.description: The last part of the file.

function.name: touch
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Create a new file of any extension in the current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the new file in the current directory. file_name is local to the current directory and does not allow path.

function.name: wc
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Count the number of lines, words, and characters in a file of any extension from current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: Name of the file of current directory to perform wc operation on.

mode.description: Mode of operation ('l' for lines, 'w' for words, 'c' for characters).

count.description: The count of the number of lines, words, or characters in the file.

type.description: The type of unit we are counting. [Enum]: ["lines", "words", "characters"]

function.name: echo
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Write content to a file at current directory or display it in the terminal.

content.description: The content to write or display.

file_name.description: The name of the file at current directory to write the content to. Defaults to None.

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.

It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Write content to a file at current directory or display it in the terminal.

content.description: The content to write or display.

file_name.description: The name of the file at current directory to write the content to. Defaults to None.

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

dir_name.description: The name of the new directory at current directory. You can only create directory at current directory.

function.name: mv
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Move a file or directory from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: Source name of the file or directory to move. Source must be local to the current directory.

destination.description: The destination name to move the file or directory to. Destination must be local to the current directory and cannot be a path. If destination is not an existing directory like when renaming something, destination is the new file name.

result.description: The result of the move operation.

function.name: pwd
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Return the current working directory path. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

current_working_directory.description: The current working directory path.

function.name: rmdir
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Remove a directory at current directory. function.name: sort
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Sort the contents of a file line by line. function.name: tail
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Display the last part of a file of any extension. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the file to display. No path is allowed and you can only perform on file at local directory.

lines.description: The number of lines to display from the end of the file. Defaults to 10.

last_lines.description: The last part of the file.

function.name: touch
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Create a new file of any extension in the current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: The name of the new file in the current directory. file_name is local to the current directory and does not allow path.

function.name: wc
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Count the number of lines, words, and characters in a file of any extension from current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

file_name.description: Name of the file of current directory to perform wc operation on.

mode.description: Mode of operation ('l' for lines, 'w' for words, 'c' for characters).

count.description: The count of the number of lines, words, or characters in the file.

type.description: The type of unit we are counting. [Enum]: ["lines", "words", "characters"]

function.name: echo
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Write content to a file at current directory or display it in the terminal.

content.description: The content to write or display.

file_name.description: The name of the file at current directory to write the content to. Defaults to None.

terminal_output.description: The content if no file name is provided, or None if written to file.

message.reasoning: Maybe the tool expects content as plain string without escape? Let's try plain ascii: "Project preliminary summary. Pending discussion." But requirement is Chinese. Maybe the tool can't handle unicode? Let's try ascii.
